incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 and L.227-1 to L.227-30 (SAS regime); implementing rules of the RCS electronic filing system.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) for the registered-office jurisdiction, operating through the national Guichet Unique portal of the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Single digital dossier for company creation containing the signed and dated Statuts (Articles of Association), the declaration of conformity (déclaration de constitution), and the certificate of publication of the legal announcement.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SAS has no legally fixed minimum share capital; the Articles freely fix the capital amount. Cash contributions must be blocked on a dedicated bank account in the name of the company-in-formation until the KBIS entry is issued when an obligation of deposit is applied; contributions in kind must be fully paid up at incorporation and independently appraised when applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned shareholders, acting in general meeting, resolve: (i) the Société par Actions Simplifiée is hereby created under the Articles of Association read and approved; (ii) the entire share capital is subscribed by the shareholders and, to the extent required, paid up in accordance with the contribution terms; (iii) the registered office is fixed at the address specified in the Articles, and the President is authorised to execute any lease; (iv) [Name] is appointed President, with full corporate authority; (v) the President shall complete all filings before the Commercial Court Registry and regulators and pay all incorporation expenses. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Legalization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary offices or the founders' legal counsel with private deed execution; notarial perfection is required for contributions in rem.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in compliance with the French Commercial Code, including corporate name, form, registered office, duration, corporate object, share capital, board provisions, and rights attached to shares. All shareholders or their duly constituted attorneys must sign each page and the final signature page. Verify that any contribution in kind has been valued and reported in the annex; if the Articles are executed by proxy, ensure the proxy powers are attached.
required_dossiers: Valid identity documents of all shareholders
Certified proxies and powers of attorney, if any
Valuation report of in-kind contributions (rapport des commissaires aux apports), where applicable
Lease agreement or address authorization for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary identifies a drafting omission or date discrepancy, the shareholders execute a supplementary rectification deed (acte rectificatif) before the same authority, and the corrected text is substituted within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Cash and Blocking of Share Capital on a Dedicated Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an account in the name of the future SAS en formation; deposit the subscribed cash capital; obtain a capital deposit certificate (certificat de dépôt des fonds) stating the exact amount. The funds remain blocked until the registry issues the KBIS. For contributions in kind, deliver the asset and execute the valuation statements in the Articles.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles or extract of share capital
Bank account opening forms and KYC declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional AML documentation, provide certified copies of bank statements and business background; alternatively, select another licensed bank and deliver the same certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Announcement (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal gazette (Journal d'annonces légales) in the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place a notice containing the corporate name, form, capital, registered office address, purpose, duration, names of shareholders exercising permanent authority, the RCS city, and details of non-cash contributions. The gazette issues a publication certificate (certificat de parution) confirming the date of publication.
required_dossiers: Details of corporate officers and shareholding
Application form of the legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette refuses publication due to inconsistent data, correct the Articles or provide a certified rectification; republish the corrected notice and obtain a fresh certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Dossier at the Guichet Unique and Commercial Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Guichet Unique formalities portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI; transmitted to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online company creation form and attach the scanned PDFs of the Statuts, capital deposit certificate, legal announcement certificate, lease or office authorization, and identity documents of officers. Pay the required greffe duties and digital fees online. The registry reviews the dossier and, if compliant, issues the KBIS.
required_dossiers: Signed and certified copy of Statuts
Identity documents of directors and shareholders
Attestations of non-conviction for the President, if requested
Foreign entrepreneur's declaration under French immigration rules, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a deficiency notice (notification de rejet), inspect the detailed grounds, rectify the concerned documents, and resubmit through the same portal within ten business days; a supplementary fee may apply after the free resubmission window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Operational Setup: KBIS, SIRET, Tax and Social Registration, and Data Privacy Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI / Greffe for KBIS, INSEE for SIRET, DGFiP for tax, URSSAF/ACOSS for employer registration, and CNIL for personal data processing declarations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the KBIS and SIRET number, synchronize company records; request employer registration with URSSAF, confirm corporate income tax reference, and appoint a registered correspondent. For the HR payroll processing scope, perform CNIL compliance steps or appoint a DPO and set up the required technical documentation for processing employee personal data. Notify the bank by providing the KBIS to lift capital blocking instructions and inform insurance brokers.
required_dossiers: CNIL/GDPR processing register and privacy policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF or tax authorities delay the employer account, request a temporary company registration certificate; if CNIL requires a prior formalities notice, file the processing declaration online and await the receipt.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; no industrial operating permit is required for an ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541214 payroll software business under French industrial installations regulations. The competent body for premises-related environmental matters is DREAL, while local municipal agencies handle public-health and fire safety matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — SaaS and software development are not ICPE-listed activities under the Code de l'environnement; no formal industrial authorization or operating permit must be obtained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion — Direction Générale de l'Aménagement, du Logement et de l'Environnement (DREAL/DEAL), supervising the ICPE nomenclature and local environmental and health regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Non-ICPE — the activity is purely clerical and data processing; no Article R.511-9 classification, no environmental authorization, and no EIA report. Office occupancy does not reach public reporting thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater is produced; sanitary sewage is discharged to the municipal sewerage network and must comply with local collective sanitation limits. Electronic waste (WEEE) and batteries are collected by approved operators under the Code de l'environnement. Printer/VOC emissions are negligible; any backup generators, if installed, must meet EU 2016/1628 emission limits and local noise requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire prevention attestation from an approved inspection body or the local fire safety service confirming that the office space complies with the French Labour Code and construction regulations. Conduct a structural load assessment for server rooms or heavy archive units, complete an occupational health and safety audit by the occupational physician, provide first aid equipment and compliance with emergency exit rules, and secure the required workplace clearance for office occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — official portal: impots.gouv.fr; business tax registration and VAT management via the professional portal 'Impôt particulier et professionnel' and the single registration system 'Gestion Unifiée de l'Immatriculation des Entreprises' / formalités-formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a French SAS must first complete corporate registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through a Centre de Formalités des Entreprises or the online Guichet Unique. The SIREN number, RCS registration, and the SIRET establishment identifier are automatically generated. The VAT identification number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) is issued by the DGFiP upon collection of registration data from the tax office; in practice the French tax authorities assign the intra-Community VAT number after the company is registered and has filed its initial existence declaration. For a non-resident company without a permanent establishment, a direct application to the DGFiP's Service des impôts des entreprises is required, and a VAT representative (représentant fiscal) must be appointed if the company is not established in the EU. The SAS should file form 11386*12 and related Beneficial Ownership declarations, and must obtain a personal identification number (numéro fiscal) to access the online 'Espace Professionnel' for filing VAT returns and corporate income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France applies entity-level taxation for SAS. The SAS is a corporate entity subject to corporate income tax on its worldwide income unless it qualifies for the territorial scope limitation for foreign permanent establishments. A French SAS may elect to be treated as a 'Société de personnes' under specific narrow rules only if it has opted for the regime of 'Transparence fiscale' pursuant to Article 239 of the CGI, which is available to certain holding entities; standard commercial SAS cannot check-the-box as a pass-through entity. Hybrid mismatch elections are governed by the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) implementation in the French General Tax Code (CGI), specifically Article 212 bis, with strict anti-hybrid rules; no general elective pass-through regime exists for a commercial SAS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,800 for sales of goods (deliveries) and EUR 36,800 for services for certain small businesses; however, the general EU distance selling threshold and the Union threshold for intra-Community distance sales is EUR 10,000 for domestic supplies to non-taxable persons when the supplier is established in France; for foreign non-established businesses, no registration threshold applies and VAT registration is required from the first euro of taxable supplies in France, subject to the Special Scheme for distance sales and the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has mandated electronic invoicing for all B2B transactions, effective 1 September 2026 for large companies and 1 September 2027 for small and medium-sized enterprises, pursuant to the Finance Law 2023. E-invoicing must be delivered through a registered Dematerialization Operator (PDP) or the DGFiP Public Portal 'Chorus Pro' using the Factur-X (hybrid), UBL, or CII formats. The transmission of transaction data to the tax administration for tax clearance is mandatory via the 'e-TVA' and 'e-invoicing' ecosystem. The fiscal clearance mechanism requires digital stamping and real-time reporting of transaction data to the DGFiP through the PDP or the public portal; each invoice must obtain a unique digital identifier and be reported in a structured data feed. Chorus Pro is not only for public procurement invoices; it is being expanded to the general mandatory domestic e-invoicing system. No physical stamp duty applies; digital validation is via invoice data transmission and the new 'Facturation électronique' reform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the European Union and intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-registered acquirer in another Member State are eligible for zero-rating (0% VAT) under Articles 262-262 ter of the French General Tax Code. The zero-rating applies only if the seller retains proof of export within 90 days for EU supplies or within the legal deadlines for dispatch. Services related to exported goods, such as freight, customs brokerage, and certain international services, may also be zero-rated if they are directly linked to the physical export. The French administration requires valid evidence of the physical movement of goods and the purchase reference; if shipping terms and documents are incomplete, the export sale is subject to 20% VAT plus penalties. Offshore services provided to a non-French business customer outside France are generally zero-rated if the place of supply rules place the supply outside France under Article 259 A of the CGI.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Document Administratif Unique / DAU) with Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (Connaissement / LTA)
Commercial invoice with export transport terms (Incoterms)
Inward Remittance Certificate / proof of international payment (relevé de remise de compte extérieur or bank SWIFT MT103 evidence)
Export delivery note with dated signature and customs seals evidence (if applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French customs and tax authorities conduct post-clearance audits of export files. If the taxpayer fails to produce the required export documentation within the statutory period or provides false documentation, the DGFiP may reassess the VAT at the standard 20% rate, apply 100% exposure to the VAT amount, and assess penalties under Article 1788 A of the CGI and Article 1737, paragraph 1 (50% penalty applicable to fraudulent VAT claims or 80% for abusive fraud). Additionally, the 'amende fiscale' under Article 1788 ter can be imposed (EUR 150 per missing proof) if the export evidence is incomplete. Criminal penalties for serious export fraud include imprisonment, fines, and potential customs fines equal to 1 to 3 times the value of the goods. The 180-day repatriation deadline is not explicitly codified as a French VAT rule; however, French tax practice requires that the payment from the foreign customer be received within a commercially reasonable period, and the failure to receive payment may trigger a written-off receivable that must be substantiated to avoid VAT clawback on the concept of taxable consideration under Article 266 of the CGI. If export documents are falsified or the transaction lacks economic substance, the VAT exemption is cancelled, the VAT becomes due, and the full legal penalties, including the 80% penalty for tax fraud, apply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank framework. Foreign-exchange and cross-border payment policy is also governed by the European Union, the French Ministry for the Economy and Finance, the French Treasury Directorate, the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, and the Autorité des marchés financiers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no general French exchange-control regime requiring prior approval for foreign-currency payments, intercompany funding, dividend remittances, loan repayments, or acquisition and disposal of foreign assets. Transactions remain subject to anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing rules, sanctions screening, beneficial-owner identification, tax reporting, transfer-pricing requirements, foreign-investment controls in sensitive sectors, and applicable European Union restrictions. A French SAS may generally remit post-tax profits, dividends, interest, royalties, and loan principal to non-residents, provided corporate approvals, distributable-profit rules, withholding-tax analysis, treaty documentation, transfer-pricing support, and bank compliance checks are satisfied. Dividend payments require legally available distributable amounts and, where applicable, approval by the competent corporate body. Banks may delay or reject payments lacking a clear economic purpose, source-of-funds evidence, beneficiary transparency, or supporting tax and corporate documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement for a resident company to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, convert a prescribed percentage into euros, or deposit export receipts into a designated domestic account. No general mandatory conversion ratio applies. Export proceeds may ordinarily remain in euros or foreign currency and may be received into French or foreign accounts, subject to banking, sanctions, customs, tax, accounting, and anti-money-laundering controls. Individual transactions may be subject to Banque de France statistical reporting, bank information requests, customs documentation, or sector-specific restrictions. Exporters should retain contracts, invoices, transport evidence, customs declarations, payment records, and reconciliation files for the applicable accounting, tax, customs, and anti-money-laundering retention periods.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
Groupe BPCE, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne entities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment accounts, SEPA transfers, collections, foreign-currency payments, and treasury sub-ledgers; not equivalent to a French bank deposit account. An offshore electronic-money institution or payment institution may serve a French SAS only if it is duly authorised in its home European Economic Area state and validly passported into France, or otherwise authorised under the applicable French and European regime. A non-EEA provider generally cannot provide regulated payment or electronic-money services into France solely through an offshore website. Safeguarded electronic-money funds are not bank deposits and generally do not benefit from the French deposit-guarantee scheme. The company must verify the provider's register status, passport notification, safeguarding model, settlement-bank exposure, EUR and foreign-currency capabilities, insolvency protections, access to SEPA schemes, transaction limits, sanctions controls, data-processing arrangements, and business-continuity provisions. Use of an EMI does not remove French accounting, payroll, tax, sanctions, AML, or corporate-record obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not generally require every director or beneficial owner to appear physically at a bank branch for account opening. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video verification, certified documents, and secure electronic signature, subject to the institution's risk policy. Banks may nevertheless require a physical meeting, notarised or apostilled documents, a French-resident contact, an in-person signature, or enhanced review where the ownership chain is foreign, the business is newly incorporated, the activity is cross-border SaaS, payment flows involve multiple jurisdictions, or the customer presents elevated source-of-funds or sanctions risk. A capital deposit account for a new SAS may be opened before registration, with the bank issuing a certificate of deposit after receipt and verification of subscribed capital. The operational account is normally activated after delivery of the registration extract and corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent beneficial-ownership information, including a nominee shareholder, multilayer foreign holding chain, unexplained control rights, or inability to identify the natural person ultimately controlling the SAS.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and residential-address evidence for directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners; board or shareholder resolutions; declarations of control; and, where relevant, certified corporate registry extracts, apostilles, translations, and trust or foundation documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed company with no operating history, no local revenue, limited capitalization, or a business plan involving substantial international payment volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; product and service description; projected cash-flow and transaction-volume schedule; customer and supplier geography; signed contracts or letters of intent; pricing model; capitalization evidence; source-of-funds evidence; tax registration information; management biographies; expected counterparties; and a written explanation reconciling projected activity with the company's industry and staffing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll and HR software model potentially involving client payroll funds, employee funds, wage payments, tax remittances, or payment collection on behalf of third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal analysis confirming whether the SAS only provides software or performs regulated payment, money-remittance, payment-initiation, account-information, or payroll-payment services; client-funds flowchart; terms of service; segregation and safeguarding analysis; contracts with licensed payment institutions or banks; prohibition of unauthorised custody of client funds; transaction-monitoring policy; refund and reconciliation procedures; and written confirmation of the regulatory perimeter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of incoming payments from unrelated foreign customers or payments routed through high-risk, sanctioned, or opaque jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer master file; beneficial-owner and sanctions-screening results; invoices and contracts; service-delivery evidence; payment-purpose mapping; country-risk assessment; transaction-monitoring rules; escalation logs; correspondent-bank information; and documented prohibition or enhanced approval process for restricted jurisdictions and counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transfers described as capital, loans, management fees, royalties, or intercompany settlements without consistent legal, accounting, and tax treatment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shareholder or intercompany loan agreement; capital-increase documentation; bank certificate; board or shareholder resolutions; general-ledger entries; transfer-pricing policy; invoices; withholding-tax analysis; treaty forms; beneficial-owner evidence; repayment schedule; and reconciliation between the payment message, contract, accounting entry, and tax filing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of wealth or source of funds for non-resident shareholders, directors, or investors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements; bank statements; sale agreements; dividend records; tax returns; investment-fund statements; loan agreements; inheritance or probate evidence; corporate transaction documents; and a signed funds-flow memorandum linking the original source to the proposed French account deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, export-control, or dual-use-technology concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identity and nationality records; sanctions-screening reports; PEP declarations; adverse-media remediation memorandum; customer and supplier screening policy; end-use and end-user statements; export-control classification; jurisdictional risk assessment; compliance-officer approval; and evidence of blocked or rejected transactions where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of virtual assets, privacy-enhancing technologies, unregulated payment intermediaries, or cash-intensive funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction history; regulated exchange records; wallet ownership evidence; blockchain analytics; source-of-funds tracing; tax treatment; AML controls of each intermediary; explanation of business necessity; and a documented policy prohibiting unidentified or unregulated funding sources.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscribed share capital through the French SAS capital-deposit account maintained with a bank or eligible depositary before registration, using the investor's account in the investor's own name where practicable. Provide the draft or executed articles, subscription form, capital-increase resolution, shareholder and beneficial-owner information, investor source-of-funds evidence, and a clear payment narrative such as equity subscription or shareholder loan. After registration, deliver the Kbis extract and request release or transfer of the deposited funds to the operational account. For subsequent injections, use SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments within the SEPA area or SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-SEPA currencies and jurisdictions. France does not prescribe a universal FX purpose-code system for ordinary commercial wires; the bank's payment-message purpose field and internal classification should accurately state equity contribution, shareholder loan, intercompany funding, or other legal purpose. Verify the sender, beneficiary, IBAN, BIC, intermediary banks, currency, value date, sanctions status, and accounting treatment. Capital increases must be supported by the applicable corporate approvals and registration or filing evidence; shareholder loans require executed documentation, arm's-length terms where relevant, transfer-pricing support, and withholding-tax review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible EUR beneficiaries, subject to scheme limits and bank availability. Use SWIFT cross-border payment messaging for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions; MT103 remains a commonly understood legacy customer-credit-transfer format, while ISO 20022 pacs.008 and related structured messages are increasingly used through bank migration programs. Include accurate originator, beneficiary, invoice, purpose, sanctions, and intermediary-bank data. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit issued or advised through a regulated bank under the agreed rules, normally UCP 600, with documents such as invoice, transport document, insurance evidence, certificate of origin, and inspection certificate as contractually required. Use documentary collections under URC 522 where appropriate. Reconcile payment, invoice, contract, customs, VAT, and general-ledger records. Do not use personal accounts, informal value-transfer systems, unexplained third-party payers, or payment splitting designed to avoid bank controls. Payroll-related client disbursements should be made only through a legally permitted and contractually documented payment structure, with client-money segregation or a licensed payment partner where required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forwards with an authorised bank or investment firm, documented under appropriate master terms and supported by an identifiable commercial exposure.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and currency-maturity management, subject to counterparty limits and applicable derivatives documentation.
Non-deliverable forwards for currencies subject to local non-deliverability or capital controls, where legally available through an authorised counterparty and suitable for the underlying exposure.
Foreign-exchange options, collars, and participating forwards, subject to suitability, valuation, accounting, liquidity, and counterparty-risk review.
Cross-currency swaps for longer-term funding or recurring currency exposures, subject to EMIR, MiFID II, collateral, reporting, clearing, and documentation requirements where applicable.

Hedging policy controls should include board-approved risk limits, permitted counterparties, eligible instruments, exposure identification, hedge documentation, valuation procedures, collateral and margin rules, segregation of duties, confirmation controls, IFRS or French GAAP accounting treatment, and prohibition of speculative trading outside approved treasury mandates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements with Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 June for calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 10,000 EUR and risk of company strike-off after 3 months of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% per month of tax due, up to 25%; potential administrative strike-off for prolonged delinquency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May for the prior calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines for non-submission and possible administrative sanctions including strike-off risk

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit required if the company exceeds two of the following criteria: turnover exceeding 800,000 EUR, total assets exceeding 400,000 EUR, or number of employees exceeding 50

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership information must be declared and updated in the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs upon any change in shareholding or control; annual confirmation is required if shareholding transfers occurred during the year

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000-15,000 USD if mandatory audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) for fiscal years opened on or after 1 January 2022; with the 3.3% social surcharge (contribution sociale sur l'IS) applicable when the annual CIT exceeds €763,000, the aggregate top marginal rate is 25.83%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate on the first €38,120 of taxable income for eligible SMEs (annual turnover ≤ €10m, share capital fully paid up and ≥75% owned by natural persons or small companies); R&D tax credit (crédit d'impôt recherche - CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenses under €100m; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% of eligible innovation expenses up to €400,000 (SMEs qualifying for CIR); JEI (jeune entreprise innovante) status granting full CIT exemption for the first profitable year and 50% exemption for the second year; application of the payroll SaaS company's headcount and HR automation R&D costs is the principal rate-reduction lever.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited forward carry (report en avant), with the annual set-off of prior-year losses capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profits above €1,000,000; optional 3-year carry-back (report en arrière) capped at €1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual CIT return (liasse fiscale): Form 2065-SD (déclaration de résultat) with the 2050–2059 series schedules (balance sheet, P&L, taxable result and annexes), filed electronically through the DGFiP professional portal impots.gouv.fr (mode EDI-TDFC or EFI).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months of the fiscal year-end; for a fiscal year ending 31 December the deadline is the second business day after 1 May (normally 3 May; postponed to the next working day if 3 May falls on a weekend or public holiday). The balance of CIT (solde) is payable on the same date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065, Box 'Résultat fiscal' (net taxable income before set-offs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregation of the company's profit before tax, after adding-back non-deductible expenses and deducting exempt items; the loss carry-forward and carry-back set-offs are disclosed in this field.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS is tax-resident in France and discloses its worldwide income; income from foreign branch/subsidiary activities must be included or covered by the relevant treaty exemption. For a non-resident parent group, no consolidation is permitted in the French liasse; each legal entity files separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs for non-deductible expenditure (e.g., excessive director remuneration, fines, 30% of certain luxury car depreciation, non-justified management fees) and deductions (e.g., prior-year losses, succession/carry-back).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees and intra-group charges paid to non-resident affiliates must be justified by a genuine benefit and supported by detailed invoices; otherwise the tax authority re-integrates them under the 'acte anormal de gestion' doctrine, increasing French taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recognition of sales of payroll automation SaaS licences, implementation fees and maintenance/HR compliance subscriptions in accordance with French GAAP (plan comptable général).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border HR payroll revenues are sourced by the French entity's residence and economic activity; transactions with non-resident group companies must be benchmarked and reported in the TP documentation attached to the return file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the research tax credit computed on eligible payroll R&D (salaries of researchers, HR automation R&D, subcontracting costs and documentation costs up to statutory caps), with supporting form 2069-A.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CIR is claimed by the French SAS on its own eligible French R&D expenditures; work conducted for a foreign parent must be carried out in France and be contractually and technically substantiated by records retained in France in case of audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2257-SD, 'Déclaration des prix de transfert' (simplified TP statement)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory annual statement disclosing the related-party transaction scheme, the list of permanent establishments abroad and the TP methodology applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required when French turnover or gross assets ≥ €50,000,000, or when the entity holds/ is held >50% by a foreign undertaking meeting that threshold; the statement must confirm the arm's length nature of intercompany SaaS IP royalties and payroll data-processing service fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the liasse fiscale: 10% automatic increase of the tax (30 days delay), 40% for bad faith, 80% for abusive/fraudulent conduct (Article 1728 CGI), plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI); late payment of the balance: 5% penalty plus 0.20% per month; Form 2257 defects: €150 per missing item of information; omissions can trigger spontaneous tax re-assessment and the 40% negligence penalty or 80% misstatement penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly CIT instalments (acomptes d'impôt sur les sociétés) - Form 2571-SD (suivi des acomptes), paid electronically via impots.gouv.fr professional services.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers: instalments due 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March of the following year; each instalment equals 25% of the CIT liability for the preceding fiscal year; due only if annual CIT exceeded €3,000 in the prior year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2571, boxes for 'Résultat fiscal de référence' (reference taxable income) and 'Montant de l'impôt de référence' (reference tax base)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determining the instalment base by reference to the previous year's assessed income and tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The instalment schedule follows the French entity's own tax result only; foreign parent's profit or loss is irrelevant to the French computation. Adjustments to the instalment amounts may be made upon assertion of loss carry-forwards, CIR or reduced-rate results.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment of each instalment: 5% late-payment penalty plus 0.20% per month late interest; the DGFiP may charge an additional 10% if the balance remains unpaid after a formal notice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory withholding on dividends distributed by a French SAS to non-resident corporate shareholders (12.8% flat income-tax withholding plus 17.2% social levies), payable through the distribution statement Form 2561; subject to reduction or elimination by the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and double-tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty/Directive relief the non-resident parent must (i) obtain a certificate of fiscal residence (attestation de résidence fiscale / certificate of residency) issued by its home tax authority; (ii) submit the certified Form 5000 (certificat de résidence) to the French paying company's tax centre before the dividend payment date to activate the simplified 'réduction à la source' procedure; or (iii) where the 30% WHT has been levied, file Form 5001 (demande de remboursement d'un prélèvement à la source) with the DGFiP before 31 December of the second calendar year following the distribution. For EU/EEA parent companies holding at least 10% of the SAS capital for an uninterrupted period of at least 2 years, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive entails a 0% dividend WHT; for DTA-covered shareholders the prompt production of the TRC and Form 5000 reduces the rate to the conventional 5%–15% threshold (0% in treaty and directive cases with 10% participation).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and licence fees paid to non-residents: domestic statutory withholding of 33.33% of the gross amount (Article 182 B CGI); EU Interest & Royalties Directive reduces to 0% for associated companies (25% direct holding for at least 2 years); DTA rates commonly 0%–10% (e.g., 5% patent royalties). Interest on commercial loans to foreign lenders: no French withholding at source on arm's-length interest (except payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions — 50% WHT, Article 238 A CGI); EU Interest & Royalties Directive grants 0% for associated companies; thin-capitalisation rules (1.5:1 debt/equity) and the 30% EBITDA interest limitation (ATAD) restrict deduction of cheap shareholder debt.
